source_unit_id: We show that the inequality~(H) can be strict for finite simple graphs.
title: Counterexamples to Hedetniemi's conjecture: strict inequality for a finite tensor product
statement_scope: Whole unlabelled main result: there exist finite simple graphs G and H whose tensor product G×H has chromatic number strictly less than min{χ(G),χ(H)}; equivalently, inequality (H) is strict for finite simple graphs. The statement is given in the abstract and introduction, and the proof includes the exponential-graph setup, Observation 1, Claim 2, Claim 3, and the final Erdős/El-Zahar–Sauer deduction. It is not replaced by the weaker partial conclusion of Claim 3 alone.

semantic_comparisons.basis: arXiv:2412.17868v3 supplies an IP-set translation lemma in additive combinatorics; its objects, hypotheses, and conclusion contain no graph tensor product, chromatic number, exponential graph, or Hedetniemi counterexample.

The firecracker/edge-corona paper studies local antimagic (total) chromatic numbers of specific graph families under a different product construction; it does not assert a strict χ(G×H)<min{χ(G),χ(H)} counterexample or use the robust-color-class construction.

The adjacent-vertex-distinguishing total chromatic number paper is the closest by the words 'graph products', but its invariant is AVD total coloring of G1 black-triangle G2, not tensor-product chromatic number; no exponential graph or Hedetniemi strictness conclusion appears.

The Discrete Analysis multidimensional Ramsey theorem concerns monochromatic product cliques in coloured Cartesian/direct products with a different quantified threshold; it does not state or prove the Hedetniemi tensor-product chromatic inequality counterexample.
The orthogonality-dimension/minrank paper on Kneser graphs uses different graph parameters and algebraic constructions; it has no finite simple graph tensor product with χ(G×H)<min{χ(G),χ(H)}.
